text:
Irene K: Heads up — AcmeCorp dedicated pool (acme-prod) is oscillating again. Customers reporting repeated 429s and 95th latency jumping to ~1.2s. Support case C-1122 opened. Graphs show a sawtooth pattern aligned with autoscaler actions: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/pool-acme

sre-oncall: @Irene K on it. Can you paste autoscaler logs and the last 20m of request rate? My first thought is noisy tenant or the cooldown is too short for this workload.

Irene K: Copy. Autoscaler tail (excerpt):
```
2026-03-17T14:02:12Z scale-up to 6 (reason: avg_qps>thresh)
2026-03-17T14:03:25Z scale-down to 3 (cooldown elapsed)
2026-03-17T14:04:30Z scale-up to 6
2026-03-17T14:05:45Z scale-down to 2
2026-03-17T14:06:50Z scale-up to 6
...repeating pattern every ~65-80s
```
Rate summary: short spikes to 1.8k rps, then drop to ~120 rps. Pool config: min_replicas=1, max_replicas=12, cooldown=60s, policy=cpu+qps. Also seeing `x-rate-limit: pool-throttle` in responses.

Sam: Quick repro from my bench using the stress harness:
```
ab -n 20000 -c 200 http://acme-prod.redwood/api/generate
```
Observed 429s during the downswing window. Response header: `x-rate-limit: pool-throttle`. Short note: request distribution is bursty (batch job origin).

Maria: Grafana snapshot uploaded. `pool_acme_utilization` shows sawtooth; `autoscaler_actions` spikes line up with scale events. Snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/snapshot/xyz123 (private)

Paul: My take: cooldown=60s is too tight for a multi-minute ramp shape — the autoscaler keeps chopping the runway. Suggest immediate experiment in staging: cooldown=300s, min_replicas=3, enable stable-window=5m and a hysteresis multiplier 1.3. Also consider tenant isolation for batch-y workloads.

sre-oncall: Agree. Plan: 1) apply the staging config (cooldown=300s, min=3) to acme-staging; 2) add a probe to detect noisy tenant `acme-batch-job`; 3) if staging looks good for 30m, propose prod change. Will kick off in ~10m and post results.

support-bot: Created ticket RT-7891 linking customer C-1122 and internal triage notes.

Irene K: Thanks. Also flagging a billing spike — Sam, can you run a token_count aggregation to see if token usage aligns with scale events?

Sam: Running now. Early result: token_count shows recurring bursts from tenant `acme-batch-job` every ~5 minutes, matching the scale spikes. Looks like a cron-ish batch that hits the pool hard then stops.

Paul: If it's a batch job, longer-term remedy is a dedicated batch pool or smoothing the batch (jitter/splay). Short-term, enabling `tenant_throttle` for that tenant or increasing min_replicas should reduce oscillation and 429s.

sre-oncall: Update: applied cooldown=300s and min_replicas=3 in staging at 14:30Z. Early telemetry (last 20m) shows reduced scale churn and fewer 429s. Will monitor until 15:00Z then propose prod roll.

Irene K: Nice. Please paste before/after graphs and the autoscaler log tail when you have them. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Will do. Tagging @oncall-night for visibility on prod rollout window.
